correctness.rationale: For a fixed acute triangle, Fagnano's unique interior orthic minimum has a positive-definite three-dimensional Hessian H, whose three rank-one chord contributions give det(H)=4∏sin²(angle)/(abc∏cos(angle)). The ellipsoid sublevel volume (2t)^{3/2}(4π/3)/(abc√detH) gives the stated sharp t^{3/2} coefficient and uniform-ball total variation law. At a fixed right triangle, direct local expansion about (X0,A,A) yields u²/h+r(φ−φ0)²/2+κ²r²/h and Jacobian √2 h^{5/4}κ^{-3/2}t^{7/4}R^{1/2}, whose half-ball integral 8π/21 gives the stated t^{7/4} coefficient and marked total-variation limit. Compactness/localization covers remainder and boundaries; limits are pointwise in parent shape, not uniform through the right angle. Independent direct-chord Hessians give K=3.224532203083055 for equilateral and 0.4261909611973396 for the inspected acute scalene example, while right small-scale ratios approach the predicted quadratic form; finite numbers are diagnostics, not asymptotic proofs.
